entries.value: Shows floating damage numbers above enemies when the player deals damage.
PerTargetTotal merges same-frame damage of one type on the same target into one number; a second damage type in the same hit is shown one line higher. PerHit shows every real damage event separately.
ScreenSpace is recommended. WorldTextMeshPro uses 3D text. Both enables both renderers for debugging. Vanilla uses the game's own damage text, the one the target dummies use.
Vanilla renderer only. On uses the game's damage type colors like the target dummies. Off keeps this mod's weakpoint colors on the vanilla animation.
Vanilla renderer only. Size of the game's damage text. 1.0 is the size used by the target dummies.

Color damage numbers by the body part hit: red for eyes, orange for heads, yellow for the thorax, white for the body and limbs. Damage with no body part, such as status effects and explosions, is white.
Show multiplier 1.0 as white instead of orange. Head hits are 1.0, so this makes them white like body hits.
Color rule used when PerTargetTotal merges several hits into one number.
Only show damage numbers on NPC targets. Keep enabled to avoid objects such as barrels.
Require sourceData.sourceUnit to exist and be the player. Disabled by default for projectiles and explosions.
Show player-owned explosions and similar secondary damage that has no weapon or melee source. Status damage over time is controlled by Show Status Effect Damage.
Show damage over time from status effects the player applied, such as burning, poison and electrocution. These are the colored numbers the target dummies show.
Final damage below this value will not be shown.
Show one decimal place for non-integer damage. Whole numbers such as 5.0 are still shown as 5. The Vanilla renderer always shows whole numbers.
How long each damage number remains visible, in seconds. The Vanilla renderer follows the game's own animation instead.
WorldTextMeshPro renderer only. Upward speed for world-space damage numbers.
WorldTextMeshPro renderer only. Scale of the 3D damage numbers.
PerHit mode only. Random horizontal world-space offset for each number, useful for shotgun pellets. Not used by the ScreenSpace renderer.
WorldTextMeshPro renderer only. TextMeshPro font size of the 3D damage numbers.
ScreenSpace renderer only. Font size for screen-space damage numbers.
ScreenSpace renderer only. Extra upward speed in pixels per second. Numbers also drift up slowly with the point above the target, so 0 does not hold them completely still.
PerHit mode and ScreenSpace renderer only. Random screen-space offset in pixels for each number, useful for shotgun pellets.
ScreenSpace renderer only. Extra deterministic screen-space spread for several PerHit numbers on the same target in the same frame. The offset is capped at 42 pixels.
Extra deterministic world-space spread for several PerHit numbers on the same target in the same frame. Not used by the ScreenSpace renderer. The offset is capped at 0.36.
Maximum active damage numbers in each enabled renderer. Clamped to 1-256, or 1-64 for the Vanilla renderer; the oldest active number is reused when full.
Maximum new damage numbers spawned in a single frame. Clamped to 1-256. Extra events are dropped to protect against hit spam.
Skip a new number when too many active numbers already occupy the same small screen area. A visual limiter only; it does not merge damage or change aggregation.
Screen-space radius in pixels used by crowding protection. Clamped to 8-120.
How many numbers may sit inside the crowding radius before a new covered number is skipped. Clamped to 1-32.
Print accepted and rejected damage events to LogOutput.log.
Press F8 in-game to spawn a test number at the screen center. The test number always uses the ScreenSpace style.
